title: A.I Adoption vs Integration
body:
I don't think most companies have an AI problem.
They have an integration problem.

I keep seeing the same pattern: the team buys the tools, everyone gets faster, and the P&L doesn't move. The tool works. The workflow around it never changed.

The numbers back this up. McKinsey's 2026 survey found 80% of people say AI made them personally more productive, but only 37% say it moved their company's EBIT. Flat year over year.

BCG puts a number on why: 10% of AIs value comes from the algorithms, 20% from data, and 70% from changing the operating model and how work gets done.

This has been most of my work lately: turning AI pilots into production systems.
Strategy first, tools second.

title: The spec is the product.
body:
Everyone’s arguing about which AI agent writes the best code.

Wrong debate.

As builders, the harder problem isn’t getting an agent to write code. 

It’s giving it a problem that’s clear enough to solve.

Instead of: “Build a login page.” 

I’d specify: “Build email/password login with validation, loading and error states. Disable submit until valid. Redirect successful logins to /dashboard. Never log passwords.” 

Now the agent has constraints to work with and I have something concrete to verify. 

That’s the shift:

You define the problem. The agent explores the solution. 

The better the spec, the fewer cycles you spend fixing misunderstandings. 

Prompts are temporary. Specs is the product.
